title: Checking Taxa Presence in Samples
text: One key challenges environmental sequencing studies determining whether detected taxa likely actually present sampling sites. vignette demonstrates use taxinfo’s occurrence checking functions validate likelihood taxa presence based known geographic distributions. taxinfo’s utilities, functions can accept either phyloseq object cleaned taxonomic names vector taxonomic names (taxnames parameter). algorithm used assign taxonomic names must stringent enough avoid false positives. Moreover, recommend using gna_verifier_pq() clean taxonomic names disambiguating synonyms correcting misspellings.

title: Checking Taxa Presence in Samples
text: main functions checking taxa presence : tax_occur_check(): Core occurrence checking function individual taxa tax_occur_check_pq(): Check occurrence likelihood within radius around samples tax_occur_multi_check_pq(): Check multiple locations simultaneously

text: Beyond occurrence data, taxinfo integrates multiple knowledge sources enrich taxonomic data Species salience public knowledge (Wikipedia), species interactions (GLOBI), scientific literature (OpenAlex), custom database content. vignette demonstrates leverage functions create comprehensive taxonomic @tax_table.

text: tax_get_wk_info_pq(): Wikipedia data page statistics tax_globi_pq(): Species interaction data GLOBI tax_oa_pq(): Scientific literature OpenAlex tax_info_pq(): Custom database integration (TAXREF, traits, etc.) tax_photos_pq(): Taxonomic images media Note: functions can work either phyloseq objects vectors taxonomic names (taxnames parameter). using phyloseq object, results automatically added tax_table. using taxnames, tibble returned.

title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: GLOBI (Global Biotic Interactions) provides data species interactions including predation, parasitism, pollination, (see rglobi::get_interaction_types() available interaction types). add interaction data focusing parasitic pathogenic relationships. plot chunk unnamed-chunk-6
code: # Get interaction data from GLOBI data_clean_globi <- tax_globi_pq(data_clean,   interaction_types = c("parasiteOf", "pathogenOf"),   max_interactions = 100 )  # View interaction columns head(data_clean_globi@tax_table[, c(   "nb",   "target_taxon_name",   "pathogenOf",   "parasiteOf" )]) #> Taxonomy Table:     [6 taxa by 4 taxonomic ranks]: #>       nb              #> ASV7  NA              #> ASV8  NA              #> ASV12 NA              #> ASV18 NA              #> ASV25 NA              #> ASV26 "2; 2; 2; 2; 2" #>       target_taxon_name                                                                     #> ASV7  NA                                                                                    #> ASV8  NA                                                                                    #> ASV12 NA                                                                                    #> ASV18 NA                                                                                    #> ASV25 NA                                                                                    #> ASV26 "Broadleaved trees and shrubs; Fagus sylvatica; Quercus; Embryophyta; Prunus persica" #>       pathogenOf         parasiteOf                   #> ASV7  NA                 NA                           #> ASV8  NA                 NA                           #> ASV12 NA                 NA                           #> ASV18 NA                 NA                           #> ASV25 NA                 NA                           #> ASV26 "; Prunus persica" "; Fagus sylvatica; Quercus" psmelt(data_clean_globi) |>   group_by(taxa_name) |>   summarise(     Abundance = sum(Abundance),     nb_inter = mean(map_dbl(nb, ~ sum(as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(.x, "; "))), na.rm = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE),     n_host_pathog = mean(map_dbl(pathogenOf, ~ stringr::str_count(.x, ";")), na.rm = TRUE),     n_host_parasit = mean(map_dbl(parasiteOf, ~ stringr::str_count(.x, ";")), na.rm = TRUE),     Guild = Guild[1]   ) |>   mutate(n_host_parasit = ifelse(is.na(n_host_parasit), 0, n_host_parasit)) |>   mutate(n_host_pathog = ifelse(is.na(n_host_pathog), 0, n_host_pathog)) |>   filter(nb_inter > 0) |>   ggplot(aes(     y = forcats::fct_reorder(taxa_name, nb_inter),     x = nb_inter,     color = Guild,     size = log10(1 + Abundance)   )) +   geom_point() +   geom_text(aes(label = paste(n_host_pathog, "-", n_host_parasit)),     size = 2.5, color = "black", nudge_y = 0.2   ) +   theme_idest() +   labs(     title = "Interactions in GLOBI",     subtitle = "First and second number indicate the number of verified taxonomic\nentity whose the taxa are respectively pathogen or parasite.",     x = "Number of interactions",     y = "Taxa",     color = "Guild following FunGuild",     size = "Number of sequences (log10)"   )

text: Get detailed interaction data analysis: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-7 plot chunk unnamed-chunk-8 plot chunk unnamed-chunk-9
code: # Get detailed interaction tibble (not added to phyloseq) detailed_interactions <- tax_globi_pq(data_clean,   interaction_types = c("parasiteOf", "hasHost", "pathogenOf"),   max_interactions = 100,   add_to_phyloseq = FALSE )  # Analyze interaction patterns interaction_summary <- detailed_interactions |>   separate_rows(target_taxon_name, nb, sep = ";\\s*", convert = TRUE) |>   mutate(across(     all_of(c("hasHost", "parasiteOf")),     ~ stringr::str_detect(.x, stringr::fixed(target_taxon_name))   )) |>   mutate(interaction_type = case_when(     parasiteOf ~ "parasiteOf",     hasHost ~ "hasHost",     .default = "other"   ))  # Visualize interaction networks ggplot(interaction_summary, aes(   x = interaction_type, y = nb,   fill = interaction_type )) +   geom_violin() +   geom_jitter(col = "grey40", alpha = 0.2, height = 0) +   labs(     title = "Species Interaction Diversity",     x = "Interaction Type",     y = "Number of Target Taxa"   ) +   theme_idest() +   theme(legend.position = "none") ggplot(   interaction_summary,   aes(x = taxa_name, y = target_taxon_name) ) +   geom_segment(     aes(       x = taxa_name, xend = target_taxon_name,       y = 0, yend = 1,       color = interaction_type,       linewidth = nb     ),     alpha = 0.6   ) +   geom_point(aes(x = taxa_name, y = 0), size = 3, color = "darkred") +   geom_point(aes(x = target_taxon_name, y = 1), size = 3, color = "darkgreen") +   scale_linewidth_continuous(range = c(0.5, 3), name = "Number of interactions") +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Interaction type") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     axis.title = element_blank(),     axis.text.y = element_blank(),     axis.ticks = element_blank(),     panel.grid = element_blank(),     legend.position = "bottom"   ) +   coord_flip() +   labs(title = "Fungal-Plant Interaction Network") library(ggraph)  edges <- interaction_summary |>   select(     from = taxa_name, to = target_taxon_name,     weight = nb, type = interaction_type   )  nodes <- data.frame(   name = unique(c(edges$from, edges$to)) ) |>   mutate(     node_type = ifelse(name %in% unique(edges$from), "Fungal", "Plant")   )  graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE, vertices = nodes)  ggraph(graph, layout = "fr") +   geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight, color = type), alpha = 0.6) +   geom_node_point(aes(fill = node_type), size = 5, shape = 21, color = "black") +   geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(node_type == "Fungal", name, "")), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +   scale_edge_width_continuous(range = c(0.5, 3), name = "Number of interactions") +   scale_edge_color_manual(values = c("grey60", "purple", "cyan", "green")) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Plant" = "lightgreen", "Fungal" = "orange")) +   theme_idest(grid = FALSE, axis_text_size = 0) +   labs(     title = "Fungal-Plant Interaction Network",     y = "",     x = ""   )

text: Integrate trait databases using tax_info_pq(). bundled trait database covers thousands genera, even small subset taxa yields informative matches. using true (larger) database, find information, even fewer taxa.
code: #> ✔ GNA verification summary: #> • Total taxa in phyloseq: 30 #> • Taxa submitted for verification: 27 #> • Genus-level only taxa: 4 #> • Total matches found: 20 #> • Synonyms: 3 (including 3 at genus level) #> • Accepted names: 17 (including 11 at genus level) #> ✔ Added 18 columns from '/home/adrien/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6/taxinfo/extdata/fun_trait_mini.csv' with information for 1 taxa in the tax_table slot of the phyloseq object # Keep only the first 30 taxa for speed (network name verification scales with # the number of taxa; the trait database still matches a small subset well). data_clean_full <- prune_taxa(taxa_names(data_fungi)[1:30], data_fungi) |>   gna_verifier_pq(data_sources = 210) # Load fungal traits database fungal_traits <- system.file("extdata", "fun_trait_mini.csv",   package = "taxinfo" )  # Add trait information data_clean_ft <- tax_info_pq(data_clean_full,   taxonomic_rank = "genusEpithet",   file_name = fungal_traits,   csv_taxonomic_rank = "GENUS",   col_prefix = "ft_",   sep = ";" ) # View trait columns data_clean_ft@tax_table |>   as.data.frame() |>   pull(ft_primary_lifestyle) |>   table() #>  #> wood_saprotroph  #>               1

text: French taxonomic data, integrate TAXREF: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-15
code: #> ✔ Added 43 columns from '/home/adrien/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6/taxinfo/extdata/TAXREFv18_fungi.csv' with information for 18 taxa in the tax_table slot of the phyloseq object # Load TAXREF data (example file) taxref_file <- system.file("extdata", "TAXREFv18_fungi.csv",   package = "taxinfo" )  # Add TAXREF information data_clean_taxref <- tax_info_pq(data_clean,   file_name = taxref_file,   csv_taxonomic_rank = "LB_NOM",   csv_cols_select = NULL,   col_prefix = "taxref_" ) #> Warning: Removed 13 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_text()`). psm <- psmelt(data_clean_taxref) |>   group_by(currentCanonicalSimple) |>   mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace(., . == "" | . == "NA", NA))) |>   filter(!is.na(currentCanonicalSimple)) |>   summarise(     taxref_FR = dplyr::first(taxref_FR),     taxref_HABITAT = dplyr::first(taxref_HABITAT),     occurence = sum(Abundance > 0, na.rm = TRUE),     Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = T),     Order = dplyr::first(taxref_ORDRE),     taxref_NOM_VERN = dplyr::first(taxref_NOM_VERN)   ) |>   filter(!is.na(Order))  ggplot(psm, aes(   x = forcats::fct_reorder(currentCanonicalSimple, occurence),   y = 1 + occurence,   fill = Order )) +   geom_col() +   geom_text(     aes(       label = currentCanonicalSimple,       fontface = ifelse(is.na(taxref_FR), "italic", "bold.italic")     ),     y = -1, hjust = 1, size = 2.5   ) +   geom_text(aes(label = taxref_NOM_VERN, y = 2 + occurence), size = 3, color = "black", hjust = 0) +   coord_flip() +   scale_fill_viridis_d() +   labs(     title = "Frequences of Taxa with French common names",     subtitle = "Bold taxa are already known in France (TAXREF).",     x = "Taxa",     y = "Number of occurences (samples)"   ) +   theme_idest() +   theme(     axis.text.y = element_blank(),     axis.ticks.y = element_blank()   ) +   scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.05)))

text: Assess information completeness across sources: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-18
code: # Calculate information completeness completeness_analysis <- data_fungi_full@tax_table |>   as.data.frame() |>   summarise(     gbif = 100 * mean(!is.na(Global_occurences)),     wikipedia = 100 * mean(!is.na(lang)),     globi = 100 * mean(!is.na(nb)),     taxref = 100 * mean(!is.na(taxref_CD_NOM)),     openalex = 100 * mean(!is.na(n_doi))   ) |>   tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "data_source", values_to = "completeness") # Visualize data completeness ggplot(completeness_analysis, aes(   x = reorder(data_source, completeness),   y = completeness, fill = data_source )) +   geom_col() +   geom_hline(yintercept = 100) +   coord_flip() +   geom_label(aes(label = paste0(round(completeness, 1), "%"), y = completeness / 2), hjust = 0.5, col = "black", fill = rgb(1, 1, 1, 0.5)) +   scale_fill_viridis_d() +   labs(     title = "Data Source Completeness",     x = "Data Source",     y = "Percentage of Taxa with Data"   ) +   theme_idest() +   ylim(c(0, 100)) +   theme(legend.position = "none")

text: Identify taxa limited information: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-21
code: # Identify knowledge gaps knowledge_gaps <- data_fungi_full@tax_table |>   as.data.frame() |>   select(Global_occurences, lang, nb, taxref_CD_NOM, n_doi, currentCanonicalSimple) |>   mutate(     gbif_info = !is.na(Global_occurences),     wk_info = !is.na(lang),     oa_info = !is.na(n_doi),     taxref_info = (!is.na(taxref_CD_NOM) | taxref_CD_NOM == "NA"),     globi_info = (!is.na(nb))   ) |>   mutate(taxref_info = ifelse(is.na(taxref_info), FALSE, taxref_info)) |>   mutate(     info_score = gbif_info + wk_info + oa_info + taxref_info + globi_info   ) |>   arrange(info_score)  # Number of available sources of information per taxa (ASV here) knowledge_gaps |>   pull(info_score) |>   table() #>  #> 0 1 3 4 5  #> 2 5 1 9 3 # Number of available sources of information per taxonomic names (current canonical simple) knowledge_gaps |>   distinct(currentCanonicalSimple, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   pull(info_score) |>   table() #>  #> 0 1 3 4 5  #> 1 5 1 7 2 # Poorly knowns taxonomic names (current canonical simple) knowledge_gaps |>   distinct(currentCanonicalSimple, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   filter(info_score <= 2) |>   pull(currentCanonicalSimple) #> [1] NA              "Xylodon"       "Antrodiella"   "Helicogloea"   #> [5] "Phanerochaete" "Auricularia" knowledge_gaps |>   distinct(currentCanonicalSimple, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   filter(!is.na(currentCanonicalSimple)) |>   ComplexUpset::upset(     intersect = c("gbif_info", "wk_info", "oa_info", "taxref_info", "globi_info"),     keep_empty_groups = TRUE,     wrap = TRUE, set_sizes = F   ) +   labs(     title = "Knowledge Gaps Across Data Sources",     subtitle = "Number of taxa names with available data from each source and their intersections"   ) + theme_idest()

title: GBIF-based Functions for Occurrence Data
text: Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) world’s largest repository biodiversity occurrence data. taxinfo package provides seamless integration GBIF specialized functions retrieve occurrence data, create distribution maps, analyze biogeographic patterns taxa phyloseq objects.

title: GBIF-based Functions for Occurrence Data
text: tax_gbif_occur_pq(): Retrieve occurrence counts GBIF plot_tax_gbif_pq(): Create distribution maps range_bioreg_pq(): Analyze biogeographic ranges tax_check_ecoregion(): Validate occurrences ecoregions tax_occur_check_pq(): Check occurrences within geographic radius Note: Functions like tax_gbif_occur_pq() tax_occur_check_pq() can work either phyloseq objects vectors taxonomic names (taxnames parameter). using phyloseq object, results automatically added tax_table. using taxnames, tibble returned.

code: #> ℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Stereum ostrea #> ℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Ossicaulis lachnopus #>  ■■■■■■■■■■■                       33% | ETA:  2s [K   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Stereum hirsutum #> ■■■■■■■■■■■                       33% | ETA:  2s  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                    44% | ETA:  2s [K   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Basidiodendron eyrei #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                    44% | ETA:  2s  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                56% | ETA:  2s [K   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Sistotrema oblongisporum #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                56% | ETA:  2s  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■             67% | ETA:  1s [K   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Fomes fomentarius #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■             67% | ETA:  1s  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■          78% | ETA:  1s [K   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Cerocorticium molare #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■          78% | ETA:  1s  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■      89% | ETA:  0s [K   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Aporpium canescens #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■      89% | ETA:  0s   [Kℹ Processing GBIF occurrences for Hypochnicium analogum #> Warning: Removed 218 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale #> range (`geom_line()`). #> Warning: Removed 22 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale #> range (`geom_line()`). #> Warning: Removed 247 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_point()`). gbif_years <- tax_gbif_occur_pq(data_clean,   by_years = TRUE,   add_to_phyloseq = FALSE ) |>   tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -canonicalName, names_to = "year", values_to = "count") |>   mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) # Visualize temporal trends for the occurences of taxa gbif_years |>   ggplot(aes(x = year, y = log10(count + 1), color = canonicalName)) +   geom_line() +   geom_line(data = filter(gbif_years, !is.na(count)), linetype = "dotted") +   geom_point() +   labs(     title = "GBIF Occurrences Over Time",     x = "Year",     y = "Number of GBIF occurrences"   ) +   theme_idest() +   ggrepel::geom_text_repel(     data = summarise(group_by(arrange(filter(gbif_years, !is.na(count)), desc(year)), canonicalName), count = first(count), year = first(year)),     aes(label = canonicalName, x = as.numeric(year)), hjust = 0,     direction = "y", size = 3   ) +   xlim(2010, 2026) +   theme(legend.position = "none") #> Warning: Removed 144 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale #> range (`geom_line()`). #> Warning: Removed 144 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_point()`). gbif_years_cumsum <- gbif_years |>   mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) |>   arrange(year) |>   group_by(canonicalName) |>   mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) |>   mutate(cum_count = cumsum(tidyr::replace_na(count, 0))) ggplot(gbif_years_cumsum, aes(   x = year, y = log10(cum_count + 1),   color = canonicalName )) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   labs(     title = "GBIF Cumulative Occurrences Over Time",     x = "Year",     y = "Number of GBIF occurrences"   ) +   theme_idest() +   ggrepel::geom_text_repel(     data = summarise(       group_by(         arrange(gbif_years_cumsum, desc(year)),         canonicalName       ),       cum_count = first(cum_count),       year = first(year)     ),     aes(       label = canonicalName,       x = as.numeric(year)     ),     hjust = 0, direction = "y", size = 3   ) +   xlim(2008, 2026) +   theme(legend.position = "none")

title: GBIF-based Functions for Occurrence Data
text: Create occurrence distribution visualizations: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-8
code: # Plot global vs regional occurrences psmelt(data_clean_gbif) |>   as.data.frame() |>   group_by(currentCanonicalSimple) |>   summarise(     Global_occurences = as.numeric(unique(Global_occurences)),     nb_seq = sum(Abundance),     nb_samp = sum(Abundance > 0)   ) |>   filter(!is.na(Global_occurences)) |>   ggplot(aes(     x = log10(1 + nb_seq),     y = log10(1 + Global_occurences)   )) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +   ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = currentCanonicalSimple),     vjust = -0.5,     size = 3,     fontface = "italic",     min.segment.length = 0.2,     force = 4   ) +   coord_flip() +   labs(     title = "GBIF Occurrence Counts vs molecular abundance",     x = "Number of sequences (log scale)",     y = "Number of GBIF occurrences (log scale)"   ) +   theme_idest()

title: Getting Started with taxinfo: Augment phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: taxinfo package provides comprehensive tools augmenting phyloseq objects taxonomic-based information various external data sources. vignette provides big picture overview package’s capabilities workflow. large part ASV OTUs, hereafter referred taxa, obtained metabarcoding studies often identified species level. taxa genus species level identification can still enriched valuable information various databases. taxinfo package allows easily integrate information phyloseq objects. Taxinfo also create body evidence presence species samples testing likelihood taxon present.

title: Getting Started with taxinfo: Augment phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: taxinfo integrates multiple authoritative data sources enrich taxonomic data: 🔍 Scientific Names Verification: Verify standardize taxonomic names using Global Names Architecture 🌍 Biodiversity Data: Access GBIF occurrence data species interactions GLOBI 📚 Knowledge Integration: Retrieve Wikipedia data scientific literature OpenAlex 🗺️ Geographic Analysis: Analyze biogeographic ranges create distribution maps

what: Using Taxnames Instead of Phyloseq Objects
title: Getting Started with taxinfo: Augment phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: functions taxinfo can work either phyloseq object vector taxonomic names. useful want query information specific taxa without phyloseq object: Key Points: - using taxnames, add_to_phyloseq parameter automatically set FALSE functions return tibbles - using phyloseq object, add_to_phyloseq defaults TRUE returns enriched phyloseq object - use physeq taxnames time - add_to_phyloseq parameter TRUE using taxnames

title: taxinfo - Augment Phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: Following Darwin core standards, key terms used taxinfo (camel case naming convention): - scientificName: full scientific name authorship date information known (e.g., “Stereum ostrea (Blume & T.Nees) Fr., 1838”) - genusEpithet: Just genus part (e.g., “Stereum”). Note correct Darwin core term genus, taxinfo use genusEpithet avoid confusion genus field phyloseq often used full scientific name. - specificEpithet: Just species epithet part (e.g., “ostrea”) - namePublishedInYear: year name published (e.g., “1838”) term come verifier globalnames (camel case naming convention): - currentCanonicalSimple: simplified scientific name without authorship (e.g., “Stereum ostrea”). correspond concatenation genusEpithet specificEpithet fields. add terms genusSpeciesEpithet: currentCanonicalSimple NA genus-names (.e. specificEpithet absent). Useful need filter unidentified--species taxa.

what: Create Species-Bound Clusters using SWARM algorithm — cluster_sbc
title: Create Species-Bound Clusters using SWARM algorithm — cluster_sbc
text: function creates Species-Bound Clusters (SBC) phyloseq object containing taxa (ASV/OTU) sequences taxonomy based proposition Riley *et al.* 2025 (). SBC (Species bound cluster) defined "clusters include ESVs assigned one species, sequence similarity threshold can vary clusters" (Riley *et al.* 2025 ). uses SWARM algorithm cluster taxa within taxnames (e.g. Genus species) based sequence similarity, allowing variable d values optimize clustering. Run swarm d=1 d=max_d, taxnames (e.g. Species binomial name), find lowest d clusters taxa assigned taxnames one cluster. taxnames represented one taxa, clustered. Taxnames containig "NA" considered unassigned. default, unassigned ASVs clustered cluster without counting taxnames. Set include_unassigned = FALSE force cluster included taxa given taxnames none unassigned ones. maximum d reached, keep clustering d print warning. strict_sbc = TRUE, taxa corresponding strict SBC clustered return phyloseq object, cases, taxa whose taxnames clustered multiple clusters whose cluster contains multiple taxnames NA cluster_ID removed phyloseq object. function returns data.frame cluster assignments optimal d value taxnames, well modified phyloseq object cluster information added taxonomy table.

title: Create Species-Bound Clusters using SWARM algorithm — cluster_sbc

Whether cluster unassigned taxa separately (default: TRUE) allow_multiple_taxa Logical. TRUE, allow clusters contain multiple taxnames (default: FALSE) regroup_cluster Logical. TRUE, regroup taxa phyloseq object based cluster_ID using [merge_taxa_vec()] (default: TRUE) tax_adjust Character vector. See ?[MiscMetabar::merge_taxa_vec()] 0: adjustment; 1: phyloseq-compatible adjustment; 2: conservative adjustment verbose Logical. Print progress messages (default: TRUE)

Can vector two columns (e.g. default c("Genus", "Species")). data_sources character integer vector. See [taxize::gna_verifier()] documentation. example, 1=Catalogue Life, 3=ITIS, 5=Index Fungarum, 11=GBIF backbone 210=TaxRef. all_matches (Logical) See [taxize::gna_verifier()] documentation. capitalize (Logical) See [taxize::gna_verifier()] documentation. species_group (Logical) See [taxize::gna_verifier()] documentation. fuzzy_uninomial (Logical) See [taxize::gna_verifier()] documentation. verbose (logical, default TRUE) TRUE, prompt messages. add_to_phyloseq (logical, default TRUE physeq provided, FALSE taxnames provided) - FALSE, return result [taxize::gna_verifier()]    function + column taxa_names_in_phyloseq depicting name    taxa phyloseq object. - TRUE return phyloseq object amended slot `@taxtable`. TRUE `taxnames` provided.    least three new columns added:    - **taxa_name**: character string sent gna_verifier (e.g.    `Antrodiella brasiliensis`)    - **currentName**: current accepted name (resolve synonym)      autorities end binominal name (e.g.      `Trametopsis brasiliensis (Ryvarden & de Meijer) Gomez-Mont. & Robledo)`.    - **currentCanonicalSimple**: current accepted name without autorities      (e.g. `Trametopsis brasiliensis`, `Russula`). columns can added depending parameters:       `genus_species_canonical_col` (adds "genusEpithet", "specificEpithet",       "genusSpeciesEpithet"), `year_col`, `authorship`. col_prefix character string added prefix new columns names added tax_table slot phyloseq object (default: NULL). genus_species_canonical_col (logical, default TRUE) TRUE three new columns added along "currentCanonicalSimple": "genusEpithet", "specificEpithet" "genusSpeciesEpithet". "genusSpeciesEpithet" identical "currentCanonicalSimple" NA "specificEpithet" NA empty (.e. genus-names excluded). year_col (logical, default TRUE) TRUE new column "namePublishedInYear" added year publication. authorship_col (logical, default TRUE) TRUE three new columns added: "authorship", "bracketauthorship" "scientificNameAuthorship". discard_NA (logical, default `TRUE`). Passed [taxonomic_rank_to_taxnames()]. problematic_chars regex pattern (character string) detect characters problematic GNA Verifier API URL. API pastes names pipe-separated GET URL path, characters like `?` (query-string delimiter), `\` (escape), `|` (pipe separator), `#` (fragment), `&` (parameter separator) corrupt URL can cause length-mismatch crash [taxize::gna_verifier()]. Names containing characters reported , `clean_problematic_chars` `TRUE`, handled verification. Set `NULL` disable detection. Default: `"[?\\#|&]"`. clean_problematic_chars (logical, default `FALSE`) `TRUE`, cells `taxonomic_rank` columns match `problematic_chars` replaced `NA` (`physeq` provided) matching names filtered (`taxnames` provided) verification. `FALSE` (default), warning issued listing problematic names sent -– likely cause error [taxize::gna_verifier()]. Set `TRUE` handle automatically, clean data upstream (e.g. [MiscMetabar::simplify_taxo()]). force_recompute (logical, default `FALSE`) `TRUE`, remove existing columns `tax_table` re-added call (.e. columns matching `col_prefix` `col_prefix` set, columns `new_cols` `col_prefix` `NULL`) performing verification. useful re-running `gna_verifier_pq()` phyloseq already contains result columns previous call. `FALSE`, existing columns left place, can cause duplicate-column errors `tax_table()` re-runs.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ df <- gna_verifier_pq(data_fungi, data_sources = 210, add_to_phyloseq = FALSE)  data_fungi_mini_cleanNames <- gna_verifier_pq(data_fungi_mini, data_sources = 210)  data_fungi_cleanNames <- gna_verifier_pq(data_fungi, data_sources = 210)  sum(!is.na(data_fungi_cleanNames@tax_table[, "currentName"])) sum(data_fungi_cleanNames@tax_table[, "currentCanonicalSimple"] !=   data_fungi_cleanNames@tax_table[, "taxa_name"], na.rm = TRUE) # 1010 taxa (71% of total) are identified using a currentName including 434 # corrected values (correction using synonym disambiguation)   tr <- rotl_pq(data_fungi_cleanNames,   taxonomic_rank = "currentCanonicalSimple",   context_name = "Basidiomycetes" )  p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "roundrect") +   ggtree::geom_nodelab(hjust = 1, vjust = -1.2, size = 2) +   ggtree::geom_tiplab(size = 2)  p + xlim(0, max(p$data$x) + 1)   psmelt(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames) |>   filter(Abundance > 0) |>   mutate(namePublishedInYear = as.numeric(namePublishedInYear)) |>   pull(namePublishedInYear) |>   hist(breaks = 100)   # Does the fungal species discovered more recently tend to be found at # greater heights in the tree? psmelt(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames) |>   filter(Abundance > 0) |>   group_by(Height) |>   mutate(namePublishedInYear = as.numeric(namePublishedInYear)) |>   ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats("Height", "namePublishedInYear") } # }

title: Get altitude range statistics for each taxa from GBIF — tax_gbif_alt
text: Retrieve altitude/elevation statistics (minimum, maximum, 5 mean standard deviation) taxa GBIF occurrence data. Two methods available: - **"gbif"** (default): Uses GBIF's Download API (`occ_download()`) retrieve occurrence records non-null elevation values. recommended approach GBIF research purposes. **Requires GBIF credentials.** - **"elevatr"**: Computes elevation GPS coordinates retrieved GBIF using AWS Terrain Tiles via `elevatr` package. provides complete coverage occurrences lack elevation data requires `elevatr` `rnaturalearth` packages.

title: Get altitude range statistics for each taxa from GBIF — tax_gbif_alt
text: ## Method "gbif" (default) method uses GBIF's Download API via `rgbif::occ_download()` following predicates: - `pred_in("taxonKey", gbif_taxon_keys)` - Filter taxon keys - `pred("hasCoordinate", TRUE)` - records coordinates - `pred("hasGeospatialIssue", FALSE)` - Exclude records geospatial issues - `pred_notnull("elevation")` - records elevation data recommended approach GBIF research purposes provides citable downloads DOIs. **GBIF credentials required.** must: 1. Register <https://www.gbif.org/user/register> 2. Store credentials `.Renviron` file:    - `GBIF_USER=your_username`    - `GBIF_PWD=your_password`    - `GBIF_EMAIL=your_email` 3. See <https://docs.ropensci.org/rgbif/reference/occ_download.html> details. Note: Downloads asynchronous may take time complete. ## Method "elevatr" method retrieves GPS coordinates GBIF occurrence records computes elevation using AWS Terrain Tiles via `elevatr` package. provides complete coverage relying GBIF's elevation field. Ocean points detected using land boundaries `rnaturalearth` reported `altitude_n_ocean` column. warning issued ocean points detected taxon. Please cite `rgbif` package. using method "elevatr", also cite `elevatr` `rnaturalearth` packages.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data_fungi_mini_cleanNames <-   gna_verifier_pq(data_fungi_mini)  # Get altitude range statistics using GBIF Download API (default) # Note: Requires GBIF credentials (GBIF_USER, GBIF_PWD, GBIF_EMAIL) # Register at https://www.gbif.org/user/register data_fungi_mini_alt <- tax_gbif_alt(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames,   add_to_phyloseq = FALSE )  # Using taxnames vector (returns a tibble) altitude_gbif <- tax_gbif_alt(   taxnames = c("Amanita muscaria", "Boletus edulis") )  # Use elevatr method to compute elevation from GPS coordinates # (provides more coverage, no GBIF credentials needed) altitude_elevatr <- tax_gbif_alt(   taxnames = c("Amanita muscaria"),   method = "elevatr",   n_coor_alt = 100,   verbose = FALSE )  # Add altitude data to phyloseq object data_fungi_mini_with_alt <- tax_gbif_alt(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames)  data_fungi_mini_with_alt@tax_table |>   as.data.frame() |>   tibble() |>   filter(as.numeric(altitude_n_records) > 100) |>   distinct(taxa_name, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   ggplot(aes(y = as.numeric(altitude_mean), x = taxa_name, fill = Guild)) +   geom_col() +   coord_flip() +   geom_errorbar(     aes(ymin = as.numeric(altitude_q05), ymax = as.numeric(altitude_q95)),     width = 0.2   ) +   geom_label(aes(label = paste0("n=", altitude_n_records)), size = 2) +   labs(     title = "Mean altitude with 5%-95% quantiles (only taxa with >100 records)",     subtitle = "Labels depict the number of gbif records with altitude data, \n     color depict ecological Guild",     x = "Taxa names",     fill = "Guild"   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") } # }

Optional inclusive year bounds used server-side filters download methods. geometry (character, default `NULL`). Optional WKT polygon used server-side spatial filter `method = "download"` (via [rgbif::pred_within()]). supported `method = "download_sql"`. clean_coord (logical, default `FALSE`). `TRUE`, run [CoordinateCleaner::clean_coordinates()] result (requires `CoordinateCleaner` package). verbose (logical, default `TRUE`). `TRUE`, print progress messages. time_to_sleep (numeric, default `0.3`). title: taxinfo (development version)
text: GBIF occurrence functions (tax_gbif_occur_coords(), tax_occur_check(), tax_occur_check_pq(), tax_occur_multi_check_pq()) now default GBIF’s Download API (method = "download"), requires GBIF credentials (GBIF_USER, GBIF_PWD, GBIF_EMAIL .Renviron). previous rgbif::occ_search() behaviour still available method = "search" (credentials, capped 100,000 records). See https://docs.ropensci.org/rgbif/articles/gbif_credentials.html. tax_occur_check() (*_pq() wrappers) now report true worldwide georeferenced count total_count_in_world taxa occurrence search radius, previous behaviour returned 0.

title: taxinfo (development version)
text: WWF/TNC ecoregion layer downloaded first use ecoregion functions (points_to_ecoregions(), tax_check_ecoregion(), tax_ecoregion_occur()) now written stable per-user cache directory (tools::R_user_dir("taxinfo", "cache")) instead inst/extdata/downloads folder created current working directory. gna_verifier_pq() removes stats main_taxon_threshold parameters. affected kingdom-level summary metadata (per-name results), main_taxon_threshold never forwarded API taxize::gna_verifier() anyway. gna_verifier_pq() gains problematic_chars parameter (default "[?\\\\#|&]") detect taxonomic names containing characters corrupt GNA Verifier GET URL (?, \, #, |, &), clean_problematic_chars parameter (default FALSE). problematic names found, warning reports count examples; set clean_problematic_chars = TRUE replace matching cells NA verification, clean data upstream (e.g. MiscMetabar::simplify_taxo()). gna_verifier_pq() gains force_recompute parameter (default FALSE). TRUE, existing result columns matching col_prefix removed tax_table re-adding , avoiding duplicate-column errors re-runs. select_taxa_pq() aborts explicit message naming requested taxnames none match tax_table, instead failing obscure OTU abundance data must non-zero dimensions error; taxa_summary_text() inherits clear behaviour. New function tax_crosscheck_pq() compares name-verification results GNA Verifier (taxize::gna_verifier() data_sources = 11, .e. GBIF Backbone Taxonomy) rgbif::name_backbone_checklist(). Returns per-taxon comparison status labels (match, mismatch, gna_only, backbone_only, both_na), summary count vector, optional Venn diagram via ggVennDiagram. Discrepancies two services highlight taxa may need manual review. tax_ecoregion_occur() gains method argument (forwarded tax_gbif_occur_coords()) keeps credential-free rgbif::occ_search() path default, ecoregion profiling wrappers (tax_ecoregion_occur_pq(), tax_check_ecoregion()) require GBIF credentials. tax_gbif_occur_coords() gains method argument ("download", "download_sql", "search") server-side filter arguments (country, year_gte, year_lte, geometry). default "download" collapses former per-taxon rgbif::occ_search() loop single, citable rgbif::occ_download() request correctly retains infraspecific higher-rank records. tax_occur_check() gains method argument ("download", "search"); method = "download" issues single rgbif::occ_download() constrained search bounding box instead rgbif::occ_search(). tax_occur_check_pq() tax_occur_multi_check_pq() now issue single GBIF download taxa (, tax_occur_multi_check_pq(), GPS points) method = "download", instead one rgbif::occ_search() call per taxon per point, expose method, circle_form, clean_coord n_occur arguments. theme_idest() falls back graphics-device default font requested font family (Roboto Condensed, Linux Libertine G, Fira Code) installed, instead failing invalid font type plot printed (example R CMD check examples pkgdown render).

title: taxinfo 0.1.2
text: range_bioreg_pq() tax_check_ecoregion() now call gbif.range::read_ecoreg() gbif.range::check_and_get_ecoreg() instead removed read_bioreg() / check_and_get_bioreg().

title: taxinfo 0.1.2
text: tax_check_ecoregion() longer takes taxa_name first argument. new signature follows package-wide physeq = NULL, taxnames = NULL, taxonomic_rank pattern. Single-species positional calls like tax_check_ecoregion("Sp.", lon, lat) must become tax_check_ecoregion(taxnames = "Sp.", longitudes = lon, latitudes = lat). return shape also changes: is_in_ecoregion always n_taxa × n_points logical matrix, full long tibble (taxon × ecoregion) counts available new taxon_ecoregions element.

title: taxinfo 0.1.2
text: Changed default behavior: add_to_phyloseq parameter now defaults TRUE phyloseq object provided, FALSE using taxnames parameter. makes workflow intuitive - working phyloseq objects, enriched object returned default.

title: taxinfo 0.1.2
text: Add points_to_ecoregions() locate set GPS points WWF/TNC terrestrial ecoregion layer. Returns tibble ECO_NAME, biome realm columns; used internally tax_check_ecoregion(). tax_check_ecoregion() rewritten thin comparison wrapper top new tax_ecoregion_occur() points_to_ecoregions() functions. now supports vector taxa (via taxnames) phyloseq object (via physeq + taxonomic_rank), always returns n_taxa × n_points logical matrix is_in_ecoregion, caches WWF/TNC shapefile across calls instead re-downloading gbif.range::check_and_get_ecoreg() time. shapefile read via sf::st_join() (boundary-safe) instead sf::st_intersection(). Add tax_ecoregion_occur() return long tibble taxon_name × ECO_NAME × n_occur × prop_occur GBIF occurrences, min_nb_occur / min_proportion filters. Zero-occurrence taxa kept n_occur = 0L downstream joins silently drop . Add tax_ecoregion_occur_pq() phyloseq wrapper tax_ecoregion_occur(). add_to_phyloseq = TRUE, three columns added @tax_table: ecoregion_top (modal ecoregion), ecoregion_n (number qualifying ecoregions) ecoregion_list (semicolon-separated, ordered descending occurrence count). Add tax_gbif_occur_coords() fetch georeferenced GBIF occurrences vector taxa (capped n_occur). Taxa zero valid occurrences listed attr(result, "missing_taxa"). tax_photos_pq() now works correctly gallery = TRUE regardless add_to_phyloseq value: add_to_phyloseq = TRUE gallery printed side-effect updated phyloseq object returned invisibly. pixture package dependency removed; gallery now built htmltools (available CRAN). Two new parameters img_height img_width replace previous h/w arguments passed via ... pixture::pixgallery(). Add fungal_traits_guilds() enrich phyloseq tax_table guild trait information FungalTraits FUNGuild databases single call. function automatically calls [gna_verifier_pq()] currentCanonicalSimple absent, optionally produces consensus columns (cons_trophicMode, cons_trophicMode_agreement) comparing two sources. main functions (gna_verifier_pq(), tax_gbif_occur_pq(), tax_get_wk_info_pq(), tax_globi_pq(), tax_info_pq(), tax_iucn_code_pq(), tax_oa_pq(), tax_occur_check_pq(), tax_photos_pq()) now support taxnames parameter, allowing users query information specific taxonomic names without phyloseq object. Added comprehensive tests taxnames parameter usage across functions. Add functions extract_spores_mycodb() tax_spores_size_pq() retrieve spore size information MycoDB. Add params year_col authorship_col gna_verifier_pq() output year publication authorship information taxa. Add function intra_taxnames_dist() compute pairwise DNA distances among taxa taxonomic names. Add function cluster_sbc() (post)cluster taxa SBC (Species bound cluster) defined “clusters include ESVs assigned one species, sequence similarity threshold can vary clusters” Riley et al. 2025 (https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-025-02284-x). Also add new vignette illustrate use cluster_sbc(). Print information using tax_info_pq() add_to_phyloseq = TRUE inform users phyloseq object updated. Add example tax_info_pq() manual EPPO database determine pest species regulated France found example phyloseq object. Change result column genus genusEpithet gna_verifier_pq() function avoid confusion “Genus” “genus” columns debug use duckdb taxinfo_pq(). gna_verifier_pq() now adds genusSpeciesEpithet column (genus_species_canonical_col = TRUE) copies currentCanonicalSimple NA genus-names (.e. specificEpithet NA empty).
